source_text: Regarding G, something I learned about today is that the concept of a catamorphism is equal to the Visitor pattern which is the same as "reduce".  This could bear on why the "shape" of a cascade matters.  Not only what you do first, but how the cascade my have recursive structure.  Keeping in mind that a pattern cascade is somehow morphogenetic; indeed, if we looked at existing *completed* missions and tasks we might be able to do "reverse morphogenesis" and figure out what cascade would have given rise to their completion.

reply_text:
I checked what the Lean does today, and your point bears on it directly: G is already a fold, but over a flat list, so the shape of a cascade never reaches it. I've written your idea and this finding into a note so it isn't lost: `futon2/holes/labs/wm-contract/NOTE-g-as-fold-2026-09-30.md` (commit `df8ca90f4`). It isn't a build plan.

**What the Lean does now.** A cascade has nodes, edges, an acyclicity proof and a precedence list. G is computed over `firing`, which is the precedence list filtered by node membership (`CascadeEFE.lean:54-56`). The computation never reads the edges. So only "what fires first" reaches G, and two cascades with the same firing order and different structure get the same G. That is the gap behind the requirement I asked codex-6 to add an hour ago, that G distinguishes arrangements.

**What the catamorphism view gives.** Suppose a cascade is a recursive structure: a pattern together with the sub-cascades it stands on, plus overlap. Then G is defined by one rule per way of building a cascade, and folding.

- **G is total by construction.** A structural recursion always returns a value, which is your requirement on G's domain.
- **Shape enters necessarily.** A different structure folds differently, including recursive structure, not only order.
- **Adjustment is local.** Adding, removing or re-nesting a pattern changes G through the rule at that one place. That is what minimising G over adjustments needs.

What gets folded is probably not a bare number. Each rule would combine how its parts change the predicted state, and G would be read off the result.

**The morphogenetic direction.** Growth is the dual of the fold: a cascade unfolds from a seed, such as the reading of a mission's HEAD. Growing and evaluating together is an unfold followed by a fold.

**One thing I can't resolve.** Your cascades are overlapping patterns, a semilattice, so sub-cascades are shared and the structure isn't a tree. A fold over shared structure has to say how a shared part is counted once. I've recorded that as open.

**Reverse morphogenesis.** For a completed mission the record exists: the turns in which it was worked (with their 象 analyses and consecutive-turn order), the commits, and the boxes ticked. From those one can reconstruct the cascade that was actually followed. I see two uses:

- **Completed work as data.** It shows which cascades, of which shape, closed which kinds of task. That is the "completed work" part of the small model you described.
- **A test of G that runs nothing.** For a completed mission, does minimising G over adjustments of its HEAD cascade come out near the cascade that in fact completed it?

A mission of that name already exists for papers: `futon6/holes/missions/M-paper-reverse-morphogenesis.md`, from April, which reconstructs problem–technique–pattern–result tuples backwards as a corpus for a forward solver. What you describe is the same move applied to the stack's own completed missions. By today's scan roughly 196 of the 337 mission files are not open. I haven't checked that count against the closed-status rule.

I haven't dispatched anything from this. It bears on two handoffs already in flight. codex-6 is adding the arrangement requirement to the Lean, and I'll point them at this note for it. The next selection handoff is computing G over the mission-HEAD cascades, and I'll frame it as a fold over structure, not over the firing list.
